title: Mallard Duck Movement
text:
Mallard ducks are among the most familiar waterfowl in Europe and North America, known for their colorful plumage, adaptable feeding habits, and broad use of wetlands, lakes, and rivers. They are highly mobile birds that often move between feeding sites, roosting areas, and breeding grounds depending on season and habitat quality.
Lake Constance is a large freshwater lake on the border of Germany, Switzerland, and Austria, surrounded by wetlands, marshes, and agricultural land that provide ideal habitat for migratory birds. The region is one of the most important stopover and breeding areas in central Europe, making it a valuable place to study bird movement.
The GPS tracking data reveal how these ducks move across the landscape, revealing patterns of foraging, seasonal travel, and site fidelity. By mapping the locations of individual birds, researchers can better understand how space use changes across time and how environmental conditions shape movement behavior.
